ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as no overcharge; no refund due — rider consented to the Sims Avenue diversion before it began (RD-3/RD-5), and the extra metered distance is not refundable where the detour is exempt.

segment_findings.reason: Driver proposed the Sims Avenue diversion before leaving the optimal route and at 12:24:05 asked 'ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?'; rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 12:24:45, i.e. the rider's own message precedes the GPS-visible divergence (~12:30–12:36) and matches the Sims Avenue/Bedok North routing actually taken. RD-5 consent to this specific route change is established; the segment is also consistent with RD-3(a)/(b) because the rider was told the location before the change. RD-4(a) has no supporting incident and RD-4(b) band 4 is only corroborative (G3), but neither is needed given RD-5.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider claims the driver took a longer way than the app showed and wants the difference back. The extra metered distance (~3.77 km: 19.24 km driven vs 15.472 km quoted) is real, but the off-route segment is exempt under RD-5/RD-3 because the rider gave prior written consent to the Sims Avenue route in chat at 12:24:45. No unexempted extra_km remains, so under RD-2 the refundable amount is 0.

Driver says traffic was building up, implying a reasonable-cause detour under RD-4. traffic.incidents is empty (RD-4(a) not met) and the only speed-band records are band 4, which under RD-4(b) and gap G3 cannot independently exempt a segment. The exemption therefore rests on RD-5 consent, not on the traffic justification.
